newsitem.title: USA: U.S. shuttle set for April 3 launch.
newsitem.headline: U.S. shuttle set for April 3 launch.

text.p: The U.S. space agency said on Thursday it had set April 3 for the launch of the space shuttle Columbia on a 16-day science mission.
NASA managers, meeting at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre, declared the space shuttle and its seven astronauts ready for flight, said agency spokesman Bruce Buckingham.
Columbia, the oldest of NASA's four shuttles, was to carry into orbit a laboratory module housing a wide range of scientific experiments, including several to study the behaviour of fire in space.
The shuttle crew was to be led by mission commander James Halsell. Susan Still, a 35-year-old U.S. Navy aviator, was to become only the second woman to serve as a shuttle co-pilot.
Mission specialists for the flight were Janice Voss, Mike Gernhardt and Don Thomas. Completing the seven-member crew were two guest scientists, Roger Crouch and Gregory Linteris.
The space agency said Thomas, who broke his right ankle during training in January, would be fit to fly.
The crew was to be divided into two shifts to keep the laboratory operating around the clock.
Columbia's lengthy mission would be the 83rd shuttle flight and the third of 1997.
